article.headline: Senators open season with a 3-2 victory over the Maple Leafs
article.description: — Stephen Halliday broke a tie at 9:46 of the third period, Linus Ullmark made 27 saves and the Ottawa Senators opened the season with a 3-2 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday night.

article.story: TORONTO -- — Stephen Halliday broke a tie at 9:46 of the third period, Linus Ullmark made 27 saves and the Ottawa Senators opened the season with a 3-2 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday night. Thomas Chabot had a goal and an assist in his first game as captain, and Michael Amadio provided the rest of the offense for Ottawa. Claude Giroux added two assists. Auston Matthews and Kirill Marchenko scored for Toronto, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 26 shots. The Maple Leafs are 1-2. Chabot opened the scoring with 1:08 left in the first period. The Ottawa defenseman joined the rush and fired a rebound past Bobrovsky. Matthews tied it 33 seconds into the second when he redirected Morgan Rielly’s point shot. Marchenko — acquired a day before the season from the Columbus Blue Jackets in a blockbuster deal — backhanded his first past Ullmark on a power play after taking a pass from Darren Raddysh at 7:06. Amadio tied it again with 7:20 to go when he finished off a 2-on-1 break with Tim Stutzle. Halliday provided the winning margin in the third just as a penalty expired. Up next Senators: At Boston on Monday night. Maple Leafs: Host Nashville on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NHL coverage here
